Author: Narendra Kumar Vyas
Bench: Narendra Kumar Vyas
 
 High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur

  Ishwar Verma S/o Shri Kancharam Verma Aged About 20 Years R/o
Village Ghutheli, Thana- Pathariya, District : Mungeli, Chhattisgarh

---- Appli
 Versus
  State of Chhattisgarh Through- P.S.- Pathariya, District : Mungeli,
 Chhattisgarh ---- Respondent

Respondent/State : Mr. Lalit Jangde, Dy. Govt. Advocate.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order on Board 20-07-2023
1.

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 14A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (for short , "the Act, 1989") against the order dated 27-4-2023 passed by the learned Special Judge (Atrocities) Act, Mungeli, District Mungeli (CG) by which the regular bail of the appellant who has been arrested on 19-4-2023 in connection with Crime No 64 of 2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 509 (B), 376, 506, 34 of IPC and Section 67 and 67(A) of the Information Technology Act and Section 3 (i)(x) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 registered in Police Station Patharia,
District Mungeli (CG), has been rejected.

2. The prosecution story, in brief, is that the complainant lodged a report in Police Station Patharia alleging therein that complainant has love affair with Ishwar Verma and complainant and prosecutrix with consent have developed physical relation and thereafter Ishwsar Verma has made obscene video and made attempt to upload the same in the group, therefore, offence under Section Ishwar Verma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64184994/
1 509(B) and Section 67 and 67(A) of the IT Act has been registered.

entities.text: Section Ishwar Verma vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: Further case of the prosecution is that the complainant has further stated that on 1-2-2023 one of the villagers has informed that obscene video has been communicated to her, therefore, it has been informed that prsent applicant has lodged complaint against Ishwar Verma.

Name of the appellant was not found in the case diary but on the memorandum statement of co-accused it has been brought on record that the same has been communicated by the present appellant, therefore, offence under Section 67 and 67(A) of the IT Act has been registered against the appellant.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that rthe complainant is a major lady and in the FIR she has stated that with consent complainant and present applicant have developed physical relation.
He would further submit that the prosecution has not collected any material to demonstrate that the obscene video was transmitted from the mobile of the present ap[ellant.
The appellant was arrested on 19-4-2023 and more than three months have been lapsed.
He would further submit that the maximu sentence which can be awarded to the applicant is five years.
He would further submit that charge-sheet has already been filed and trial wil take considerable time folr its conclusion, therefore the appellant is entitled to be realsed on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposing the bail application would submit that the appellant was involved in the offence of Section 376 of IPC and other offences.
He would further submit that henious offence has been committed by the appellant, therefore, he would pray for rejection of the bail.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the partiesand perused the record.

6. Perusal of the case diary goes to show that the complainant is a major lady and in the FIR she has stated that with consent of the prsent applciant, physical relation was developed and also considering the fact that the both complainant and appellant are majors, therefore, offence under Section 376 of IPC would not be made out, whereas in the statement recorded under section 164 of the Cr.P:.C., complainant stated that present applicant has threatened her, therefore, physical relation has been developed.

7. Considering the fact that the complainant is a major lady, there are omissions & contradictions in her statement in FIR and 164 of Cr.P.C., statement and further consdierieng the medical opinion given by the Doctor wherein it has been mentioned that no injury was found in her private part and there is no definite opinion regarding commission of offence and also considering the fact that the charge sheet has been filed, the appellant is in jail since 19-4-2023 and trial will take consdierable time, I am inclined to release the appellant on bail.
8.
Accordingly, the instant criminal appeal is allowed and the order dated 27-4-2023 (Annexure A/1) passed by the court below is set aside.

The appellant is directed to be released on bail on his executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.25,000/- with one local surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the said Court as and when directed.
